items.name: The generalized Kottwitz conjecture (statement)
items.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite, G/F connected reductive, b ∈ G(F̆) basic, G_b its inner form, μ a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_F̄ with field of definition E, [b] the basic class of B(G, μ), ℓ ≠ p. For a supercuspidal parameter φ: W_F → ^LG and ρ ∈ Π_φ(G_b), the conjecture asserts the equality in Groth(G(F) × W_E) Mant_{b,μ}(ρ) = Σ_{π∈Π_φ(G)} π ⊠ Hom_{S_φ}(δ_{π,ρ}, r_μ∘φ_E), where r_μ is the irreducible representation of ^LG_E of highest weight μ and r_μ∘φ_E(s, w) = r_μ(s·φ(w)) on S_φ × W_E. It extends Kottwitz's conjecture (Rapoport; Rapoport–Viehmann Conjecture 7.3) to non-minuscule μ and to G not a B-inner form of its quasi-split form.

items.name: Theorem 1.0.2(1): the Kottwitz conjecture on the elliptic locus
items.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite, G/F connected reductive, b ∈ G(F̆) basic, G_b its inner form, μ a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_F̄ with field of definition E, [b] the basic class of B(G, μ), ℓ ≠ p. Assume the refined local Langlands correspondence (Kaletha, Conjecture G). Let φ: W_F × SL_2 → ^LG be a discrete parameter with Q̄_ℓ-coefficients and ρ ∈ Π_φ(G_b). Ignoring the W_E-action, Mant_{b,μ}(ρ) = Σ_{π∈Π_φ(G)} dim Hom_{S_φ}(δ_{π,ρ}, r_μ)·π + err in Groth(G(F)), where err ∈ Groth(G(F)) is a virtual representation whose character vanishes on the elliptic locus of G(F).
items.locator: Theorem 1.0.2, p. 4; restated as Theorem 6.5.1, p. 65, and proved in Section 6.5

items.name: Theorem 1.0.2(2): vanishing of the error term
items.statement: In Theorem 1.0.2, if the packet Π_φ(G) consists of supercuspidal representations and the Fargues–Scholze semisimple parameter φ_ρ of ρ is supercuspidal, then err = 0.
items.locator: Theorem 1.0.2, p. 4; second paragraph; Theorem 6.5.1, p. 65

items.name: Theorem 1.0.3: Fargues–Scholze parameters for inner forms of GL_n
items.statement: Let G be any inner form of GL_n/F and π an irreducible smooth representation of G(F). Then the L-parameter φ_π attached to π by Fargues–Scholze (§I.9) agrees with the usual semisimplified L-parameter of π.
items.locator: Theorem 1.0.3, p. 5; restated as Theorem 6.6.1, p. 69
items.note: For G = GL_n itself this is Fargues–Scholze IX.7.4, planned at ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES7:GLn-comparison (item 005); the inner forms are new.

items.name: Fargues–Scholze parameters agree with local Langlands for GL_n
items.statement: For G = GL_n/F, the Fargues–Scholze parameter of every irreducible smooth Q̄_ℓ-representation is the Weil semisimplification of its classical local Langlands parameter (Fargues–Scholze, Theorem I.9.6(ix) and IX.7.4).
items.locator: Theorem 6.6.1, p. 69; proof, p. 69 (cited as [FS21, Theorem I.9.6.viii–ix])

items.name: B(G, μ), basic classes, decent representatives and the inner forms G_b
items.statement: For b ∈ G(F̆), G_b(F) = {g ∈ G(F̆) : Ad(b)σ(g) = g}, depending on [b] only; b may be chosen decent (Rapoport–Zink 1.8), so b ∈ G(F') for F'/F finite unramified; the slope morphism ν_b is defined over F', its centralizer is a Levi, and G_b is an inner form of a Levi M^* of G^* (Kottwitz 1997 §§3–4). b is basic iff M^* = G^*, and B(G)_basic ≅ X^*(Z(Ĝ)^Γ) (Kottwitz 1985, Proposition 5.6), giving λ_b.

items.name: Kottwitz's Galois gerbe description of B(G) and the rigid comparison map
items.statement: Inflation gives B(G) = H^1(⟨σ⟩, G(F̆)) ≅ H^1(W_F, G(L̄)); a section W_F → ℰ of Kottwitz's Galois gerbe 1 → D(F̄) → ℰ → Γ → 1 induces isomorphisms H^1_alg(ℰ, G(F̄)) ≅ B(G) and H^1_bas(ℰ, G(F̄)) ≅ B(G)_bas independent of the section (Kottwitz 1997 §8 and App. B; Kottwitz, B(G) for all local and global fields). Kaletha's map H^1_bas(ℰ, G(F̄)) → H^1(u → W, Z(G) → G) (Kaletha, rigid inner forms vs isocrystals, §3.3) compares with rigid inner forms; for a basic cocycle z_b there is g ∈ G(L̄), unique up to G_b(F), with g^{-1}z_b(w)w(g) = b·σ(b)⋯σ^{|w|−1}(b), and Ad(g): G_{z_b} ≅ G_b over F.

items.name: Rigid inner forms and the enlarged Tate–Nakayama isomorphism
items.statement: For finite central Z ⊆ G^* over F, Kaletha's H^1(u → W, Z → G^*); their colimit H^1(u → W, Z(G^*) → G^*) (injective transitions); surjectivity onto H^1(F, G^*_ad) (Kaletha, rigid inner forms, Corollary 3.8), so an inner twist ψ lifts to a rigid inner twist (ψ, z); and the Tate–Nakayama isomorphism H^1(u → W, Z(G^*) → G^*) ≅ π_0(Z(\hat{\bar G})^+)^* (ibid., Corollary 5.4), giving characters λ_z, λ_{z_b}.
items.note: The Kaletha 2016 extraction proposes a Part II of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison for rigid inner forms (pending review); if accepted it owns this item.

items.name: The refined local Langlands correspondence (Kaletha, Conjecture G) as a hypothesis
items.statement: For each tempered (here discrete) parameter φ: a finite L-packet Π_φ of representations of rigid inner forms of G; for a Whittaker datum 𝔴 of G^*, a unique 𝔴-generic member; bijections Π_φ(G) ≅ Irr(π_0(S_φ^+), λ_z) and Π_φ(G_{z_b}) ≅ Irr(π_0(S_φ^+), λ_z + λ_{z_b}), π ↦ τ_{z,𝔴,π}; and the endoscopic character identities, which characterize these bijections. For B-inner forms this implies the isocrystal version (Conjecture F; Kaletha 2018).
items.locator: Section 1, p. 2; p. 3, items 1–4; Sections 2.2–2.3 and A.1
items.note: Status of the conjecture (Introduction, pp. 3–4): known for regular supercuspidal parameters when G splits over a tame extension, char F = 0 and p ≥ (e+2)n (Kaletha 2019; Fintzen–Kaletha–Spice). The rigid-inner-form owner is pending (see item 008).

items.name: The groups S_φ^+ and Z(\hat{\bar G})^+ through the universal cover of Ĝ
items.statement: With Z_n ⊆ Z(G) the elements whose image in Z(G)/Z(G_der) is n-torsion and G_n = G/Z_n = G_ad × C_n, \hat{\bar G} = lim \hat G_n = \hat G_sc × \hat C_∞ is the universal cover of Ĝ; Z(\hat{\bar G})^+ ⊆ S_φ^+ ⊆ \hat{\bar G} are the preimages of Z(Ĝ)^Γ ⊆ S_φ = Cent(φ, Ĝ); Rep(π_0(S_φ^+), λ) and Irr(π_0(S_φ^+), λ) denote the λ-isotypic representations.

items.name: From S_φ^+ back to S_φ
items.statement: The map S_φ^+ → S_φ, (a, (b_n)) ↦ a_der·b_1/N_{E/F}(b_{[E:F]}) (Kaletha 2018, (4.7); independent of the large Galois E/F) induces by pullback a bijection Rep(π_0(S_φ^+), λ_{z_b}) ≅ Rep(S_φ, λ_b), restricting to irreducibles (ibid., Lemma 4.1, valid without irreducibility; S_φ^♮ = S_φ for discrete φ).

items.name: The relative position δ_{π,ρ} for B-inner forms
items.statement: If G is a B-inner form of G^* (some ψ ∈ Ψ with decent basic b^* and ψ^{-1}σ(ψ) = Ad(b^*)), the isocrystal refined LLC gives Π_φ(G) ≅ Irr(S_φ, λ_{b^*}) and Π_φ(G_b) ≅ Irr(S_φ, λ_{b^*} + λ_b), and δ_{π,ρ} := τ̌_{b^*,𝔴,π} ⊗ τ_{b^*,𝔴,ρ} ∈ Rep(S_φ, λ_b).

items.name: The relative position δ_{π,ρ} in general
items.statement: δ_{π,ρ} ∈ Rep(S_φ, λ_b) is the image of τ̌_{z,𝔴,π} ⊗ τ_{z,𝔴,ρ} ∈ Rep(π_0(S_φ^+), λ_{z_b}) under the bijection Rep(π_0(S_φ^+), λ_{z_b}) ≅ Rep(S_φ, λ_b) (ρ identified with ρ∘Ad(g) on G_{z_b}(F)); for B-inner forms it agrees with the definition of Section 2.2.

items.name: δ_{π,ρ} does not depend on the choices
items.statement: Assuming Kaletha's Conjecture G, δ_{π,ρ} is independent of the Whittaker datum 𝔴 and of the rigidifying cocycle z ∈ Z^1(u → W, Z(G^*) → G^*) (changing 𝔴 twists τ by a character (𝔴, 𝔴') of π_0(S_φ/Z(Ĝ)^Γ); Kaletha, Genericity Theorem 4.3, and rigid inner forms vs isocrystals, Lemma 6.2).

items.name: Local shtuka spaces with one leg
items.statement: Sht_{G,b,μ} sends a perfectoid C-algebra (R, R^+) to the isomorphisms γ: E^1|_{X_{R♭}∖D_R} ≅ E^b|_{X_{R♭}∖D_R} of G-torsors meromorphic along D_R and bounded by μ pointwise (relative position in G(B_dR^+)\G(B_dR)/G(B_dR^+) dominated by μ); it is a locally spatial diamond with commuting G(F)- and G_b(F)-actions, recovering Scholze's infinite-level space (Scholze–Weinstein 23.2.2), and for μ minuscule it is the diamond of a local Shimura variety of dimension ⟨μ, 2ρ_G⟩.

items.name: Compactly supported cohomology of local shtuka spaces with Satake coefficients
items.statement: For K ⊆ G(F) compact open, Sht_{G,b,μ,K} = Sht_{G,b,μ}/K is a locally spatial diamond; with S_{μ,n} the Satake object of the Weyl module V_{μ,n} ∈ Rep(Ĝ, Z/ℓ^n), RΓ_c(Sht/K, S_μ) := colim_U lim_n RΓ_c(U, S_{μ,n}) over quasi-compact opens U, a complex of Z_ℓ[√q]-modules with G_b(F) × W_E-action.

items.name: The functor RΓ(G, b, μ)[ρ] and the Mantovan map
items.statement: For ρ a finite-length admissible Q̄_ℓ-representation of G_b(F), RΓ(G, b, μ)[ρ] := colim_{K⊆G(F)} RHom_{G_b(F)}(RΓ_c(Sht/K, S_μ) ⊗ Q̄_ℓ, ρ), a finite-length W_E-equivariant object of the derived category of smooth G(F)-representations (Proposition 6.4.5); Mant_{b,μ}: Groth(G_b(F)) → Groth(G(F) × W_E) sends ρ to its Euler characteristic.

items.name: Comparison with Rapoport–Viehmann's normalization
items.statement: For μ minuscule, S_μ = Z_ℓ[√q][d](d/2) with d = ⟨μ, 2ρ_G⟩, there is a spectral sequence H^{i,j−d}(G, b, μ)[ρ](−d/2) ⇒ H^{i+j}(RΓ(G, b, μ)[ρ]) with H^{i,j}[ρ] = colim_K Ext^i_{G_b(F)}(H^j_c(M_{G,b,μ,K}, Z_ℓ) ⊗ Q̄_ℓ, ρ), and Mant_{b,μ}(ρ) = (−1)^d H^*(G, b, μ)[ρ](d/2) with Rapoport–Viehmann's H^*(G, b, μ)[ρ].

items.name: Regular semisimple, strongly regular and elliptic elements
items.statement: G_rs ⊆ G is the open subvariety of regular semisimple elements (connected centralizer a maximal torus), G_sr ⊆ G_rs the strongly regular ones (centralizer a maximal torus), G(F)_ell ⊆ G(F)_sr those with elliptic centralizer; G(F)_ell ⊆ G(F)_sr ⊆ G(F)_rs, the middle inclusion dense; regular semisimple g satisfies α(g) ≠ 1 for all roots.

items.name: The space of regular semisimple conjugacy classes is locally profinite
items.statement: G(F)_rs//G(F) is locally profinite, the disjoint union of T(F)_rs/N(T, G)(F) over G(F)-conjugacy classes of F-rational maximal tori T; the same holds for sr. (The map (g, t) ↦ gtg^{-1}: G(F) × T_rs(F) → G_rs(F) is a submersion, hence open, so the torus class is locally constant.)
items.note: See source issue E3 for a misstatement in the proof.

items.name: Stably conjugate strongly regular elements are conjugate over F̆
items.statement: If g ∈ G(F) and g' ∈ G_b(F) are strongly regular and conjugate over an algebraic closure of F̆, they are conjugate over F̆ (Steinberg: H^1(F̆, T) = 0 for the torus T = Cent(g, G)); such g, g' are called related.

items.name: The isocrystal invariant of related elements
items.statement: For related strongly regular g ∈ G(F)_sr, g' ∈ G_b(F)_sr with g' = ygy^{-1}, y ∈ G(F̆), and T = Cent(g, G), inv[b](g, g') is the class of y^{-1}bσ(y) ∈ T(F̆) in B(T).

items.name: Properties of the isocrystal invariant
items.statement: inv[b](g, g') ∈ B(T) depends only on b, g, g' (not on y); inv[b](Ad(z)g, g') = Ad(z)(inv[b](g, g')) for z ∈ G(F) and inv[b](g, Ad(z')g') = inv[b](g, g') for z' ∈ G_b(F); and its image under B(T) → B(G) → π_1(G)_Γ is κ(b) (Kaletha, Supercuspidal L-packets via isocrystals).

items.name: The relation space Rel_b
items.statement: Rel_b is the set of conjugacy classes (under G(F) × G_b(F)) of triples (g, g', λ) with g ∈ G(F)_sr, g' ∈ G_b(F)_sr related and λ ∈ X_*(T), T = Cent(g, G), such that κ(inv[b](g, g')) is the image of λ in X_*(T)_Γ; it carries the subspace topology of (G(F) × G_b(F) × X_*(G))/(G(F) × G_b(F)), with projections to G(F)_sr//G(F) and G_b(F)_sr//G_b(F).

items.name: A cocharacter and g determine the related class
items.statement: Given g ∈ G(F)_sr and λ ∈ X_*(Cent(g, G)), there is at most one G_b(F)-conjugacy class of g' with (g, g', λ) ∈ Rel_b: g and inv[b](g, g') determine the class of g'.

items.name: Rel_b is a local homeomorphism onto an open and closed set
items.statement: Rel_b → G(F)_sr//G(F) is a homeomorphism locally on the source, with image the classes that transfer to G_b, which is open and closed; likewise for Rel_b → G_b(F)_sr//G_b(F).

items.name: Hecke transfer maps
items.statement: Let r_μ be the Weyl module of Ĝ of highest weight μ̂, r_μ[λ] its λ̂-weight space and d = ⟨μ, 2ρ_G⟩. For Λ with p invertible, T^{G→G_b}_{b,μ}: C(G(F)_sr//G(F), Λ) → C(G_b(F)_sr//G_b(F), Λ), [T f](g') = (−1)^d Σ_{(g,g',λ)∈Rel_b} f(g) dim r_μ[λ], and symmetrically T^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}; the sums are finite and compact support is preserved.

items.name: The transfer vanishes unless [b] is the basic class of B(G, μ)
items.statement: T^{G→G_b}_{b,μ} = 0 unless [b] is the unique basic class of B(G, μ) (a nonzero r_μ[λ] forces λ and μ to have equal image in π_1(G)_Γ, which equals κ(b)). In that case the kernel is supported on the truncation Rel_{b,μ} (λ ≤ μ), and both maps Rel_{b,μ} → G(F)_sr//G(F), G_b(F)_sr//G_b(F) are finite étale over their images.
items.locator: Lemma 3.2.8, p. 15; and the paragraph after it, p. 16

items.name: Theorem 3.2.9: the endoscopic trace relation
items.statement: Assume b ∈ B(G, μ) basic, Λ an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 abstractly isomorphic to C, and Kaletha's Conjecture G. Let φ be a discrete L-parameter with Λ-coefficients and ρ ∈ Π_φ(G_b) with Harish-Chandra character Θ_ρ. Then for every g ∈ G(F)_sr that transfers to G_b(F), [T^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}Θ_ρ](g) = Σ_{π∈Π_φ(G)} dim Hom_{S_φ}(δ_{π,ρ}, r_μ)·Θ_π(g).
items.locator: Theorem 3.2.9, p. 16; equation (3.2.3); proved in Section 3.3

items.name: The GL_2 example: Theorem 3.2.9 is the Jacquet–Langlands identity
items.statement: For G = GL_2, μ(x) = diag(x, 1), b the basic class of slope 1/2 (G_b(F) the units of the quaternion division algebra), S_φ = Z(Ĝ) and dim Hom(δ_{π,ρ}, r_μ) = 2, while T^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}f'(g) = −2f'(g'); so Theorem 3.2.9 reduces to Θ_ρ(g') = −Θ_π(g).
items.note: The printed example writes T^{G→G_b} and f = Θ_ρ; see source issue E4.

items.name: The sign identity e(G)e(G_b) = (−1)^{⟨2ρ_G, μ⟩}
items.statement: For [b] ∈ B(G, μ) basic, the Kottwitz signs satisfy e(G)e(G_b) = (−1)^{⟨2ρ_G, μ⟩} (from Lemma A.2.1: the inner twists G^* → G, G^* → G_b correspond to μ_1, μ_2 ∈ X^*(Z(Ĝ_sc)^Γ) with μ_2 − μ_1 the image of κ(b), which is that of μ).

items.name: Compatible Haar measures on inner forms and related tori
items.statement: An element η ∈ ∧^{dim G}(Lie(G)^*)(F̆) defines a Λ-valued Haar measure on G(F) (rescale by a ∈ O_F̆^× into the F-points); via G_F̆ = (G_b)_F̆ this gives compatible measures on G(F) and G_b(F), and via admissible isomorphisms Ad(g), g ∈ G(F̆) unique up to N(T_1, G)(F̆) acting through an O^×-valued character, compatible measures on related maximal tori.

items.name: Orbital integrals identify coinvariants with invariant functions
items.statement: For φ ∈ C_c(G(F)_sr, Λ), the orbital integral φ_G(y) = ∫_{G(F)/G(F)_y} φ(xyx^{-1}) dx induces an isomorphism C_c(G(F)_sr, Λ)_{G(F)} ≅ C_c(G(F)_sr//G(F), Λ).

items.name: The stable Weyl integration formula
items.statement: For f ∈ C(G(F)_sr//G(F), Λ) and φ ∈ C_c(G(F)_sr, Λ), ∫_{G(F)} f φ dx = ⟨f, φ_G⟩_G with ⟨f, h⟩_G = Σ_T |W(T, G)(F)|^{-1} ∫_{T(F)_sr} |D(t)| Σ_{t_0∼t} f(t_0)h(t_0) dt, T over stable classes of maximal tori, D(t) = det(Ad(t) − 1 | Lie G/Lie T) and t_0 over the G(F)-classes in the stable class of t.

items.name: Adjointness of the Hecke transfer maps
items.statement: For f' ∈ C(G_b(F)_sr//G_b(F), Λ) and f ∈ C(G(F)_sr//G(F), Λ), one compactly supported, ⟨T^{G_b→G}_{b,μ} f', f⟩_G = ⟨f', T^{G→G_b}_{b,μ} f⟩_{G_b}.

items.name: Harish-Chandra characters
items.statement: For a finite-length admissible representation π of G(F) (char F = 0, coefficients C ≅ Λ), the trace distribution of π is represented on G(F)_sr by a locally constant conjugation-invariant function Θ_π ∈ C(G(F)_sr//G(F), Λ), its Harish-Chandra character, and a virtual representation is non-elliptic if Θ vanishes on G(F)_ell.
items.locator: Theorem 3.2.9, p. 16; statement; also Theorem 6.5.2, p. 65, and Section C.1, p. 75

items.name: Six operations and base change for maps representable in nice diamonds
items.statement: Call f: Y → X of small v-stacks nice if it is compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds and locally of finite dim.trg. For such f there are Rf_! ⊣ Rf^! with (P1) f^*A ⊗ f^*B ≅ f^*(A ⊗ B), (P2) Rf_*RHom(f^*A, B) ≅ RHom(A, Rf_*B), (P3) projection formula, (P4) RHom(Rf_!A, B) ≅ Rf_*RHom(A, Rf^!B), (P5) Rf^!RHom(A, B) ≅ RHom(f^*A, Rf^!B), and base change (BC1) g^*Rf_! ≅ Rf'_!g̃^* for f nice, (BC2) Rg^!Rf_* ≅ Rf'_*Rg̃^! for g nice (Scholze, ECD Theorems 1.8–1.9).

items.name: Cohomological smoothness and smooth base change
items.statement: For f nice, the natural map Rf^!Λ ⊗ f^* → Rf^! is an equivalence when f is cohomologically smooth, Rf^!Λ is then invertible (étale locally L[n]), and for f cohomologically smooth g̃^*Rf^! ≅ Rf'^!g^* and f'^*Rg^! ≅ Rg̃^!f^* (ECD Theorem 1.10).

items.name: Decent v-stacks and fine morphisms (Gulotta–Hansen–Weinstein)
items.statement: A decent v-stack is a small v-stack X whose diagonal is representable in locally separated locally spatial diamonds and which admits a chart: a strictly surjective map U → X from a locally separated locally spatial diamond, representable in locally spatial diamonds and locally compactifiable of finite dim.trg and cohomologically smooth. f: X → Y is fine if it lifts to charts W → V locally compactifiable of finite dim.trg. Locally separated locally spatial diamonds (e.g. X^♢ for analytic adic X) are decent; decent v-stacks are Artin v-stacks; products and fibre products of decent v-stacks are decent; fine maps are stable under composition and base change; nice maps are fine.
items.locator: Definition 4.1.7, p. 23; and the list after it, p. 24

items.name: The !-functors for fine maps of decent v-stacks (Gulotta–Hansen–Weinstein)
items.statement: For every fine map f: Y → X of decent v-stacks there are functors Rf_! and Rf^! satisfying (P1)–(P5) and (BC1)–(BC2), agreeing with Scholze's for nice f, pseudo-functorial in f, with Rf_! ≅ Rf_* pseudo-naturally for proper f; cohomological smoothness extends to fine maps (intrinsically or via charts) with Rf^!Λ ⊗ f^* ≅ Rf^! and smooth base change.
items.locator: Theorem 4.1.8, p. 24; citing Gulotta–Hansen–Weinstein, Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 4.17

items.name: Relative dualizing complexes and integration
items.statement: For f: X → S fine between decent v-stacks, K_{X/S} = Rf^!Λ; for S connected and f proper, the counit Rf_*K_{X/S} = Rf_!Rf^!Λ → Λ induces ω ↦ ∫_X ω: H^0(X, K_{X/S}) → Λ.

items.name: Upper-shriek and invertible objects
items.statement: For f fine and I ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) invertible, Rf^!A ⊗ f^*I → Rf^!(A ⊗ I) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Dualizing complexes of the diagonal are inverse
items.statement: For f: Y → X fine and cohomologically smooth, RΔ^!_{Y/X}Λ_{Y×_XY} ⊗ Rf^!Λ_X ≅ Λ_Y canonically, so K_{Y/Y×_XY} ≅ K_{Y/X}^{-1} is invertible.

items.name: Sheaves on constant locally profinite diamonds
items.statement: Over S = Spd C or Spd k (geometric points), for T locally profinite and f: T_S = T × S → S, D_ét(T_S, Λ) is the derived category of smooth C(T, Λ)-modules (Λ ↦ C_c(T, Λ)); f^*M = C_c(T, Λ) ⊗ M, f_*M = M^c, f_!M = M, f^!M = RHom(C_c(T, Λ), M)^s, and H^0(T_S, f^!Λ) = Dist(T, Λ).

items.name: Classifying stacks of locally pro-p groups
items.statement: For G locally pro-p admitting a free action on a separated locally spatial diamond strictly surjective and cohomologically smooth over S (e.g. G ⊆ GL_n(E) closed), [S/G_S] is decent; q: S → [S/G_S] is nice, q^* identifies D_ét([S/G_S], Λ) with the derived category of smooth G-representations (Fargues–Scholze V.1.1), q_*M = C(G, M)^{G-sm}, q_!M = C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ M, q^!M = Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ), M) and q^!Λ = Haar(G, Λ).

items.name: Restriction and induction as operations on classifying stacks
items.statement: For H ⊆ G closed and q: [S/H_S] → [S/G_S], q^* is restriction, q_* smooth induction Ind_H^G, q_! compact induction cInd_H^G, q^! = q^* for H open, and q^!M = Hom_{H'}(C_c(H', Λ), M)^{H-sm} when G = H × H'.

items.name: The structure map of a classifying stack
items.statement: f: [S/G_S] → S is fine and cohomologically smooth, with f^*M = M (trivial action), f_*M = RΓ(G, M), f_!M = (M ⊗ Haar(G, Λ))_G (homology twisted by Haar measures), f^!M = Haar(G, Λ)^* ⊗ M and K_{[S/G_S]/S} = Haar(G, Λ)^*.

items.name: Quotients of locally profinite sets by locally pro-p groups
items.statement: For T locally profinite with continuous G-action, [T_S/G_S] is decent and fine over S, D_ét([T_S/G_S], Λ) is the derived category of G-equivariant smooth C(T, Λ)-modules, and H^0([T_S/G_S], K) ≅ Hom_G(C_c(T, Λ) ⊗ Haar(G, Λ), Λ); for G unimodular with a chosen Haar measure this is Dist(T, Λ)^G.

items.name: Dualizable objects and categorical traces in symmetric monoidal 2-categories
items.statement: An object X of a symmetric monoidal 2-category (𝒞, ⊗, 1) is dualizable if there are X^∨, ev: X^∨ ⊗ X → 1 and coev: 1 → X ⊗ X^∨ with the two zig-zag composites isomorphic to identities; then X^∨ ⊗ Y = iHom(X, Y). The categorical trace of f ∈ End X is tr(f) = ev∘(f ⊗ id)∘coev ∈ Ω𝒞 = End(1) (Lu–Zheng, Definition 1.1, Construction 1.6).
items.note: Mathlib's CategoryTheory.ExactPairing and HasRightDual (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Basic.lean:77, :236) give the 1-categorical duality data but not traces in symmetric monoidal 2-categories. The Abe extraction proposes the same generic interface in EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartIIRelativeTraces (still a proposal); if that is accepted, this item should be imported from it.

items.name: Dualizable objects of D(Λ)
items.statement: For any ring Λ, M ∈ D(Λ) is dualizable iff it is a perfect complex, with dual RHom(M, Λ), and the categorical trace of an endomorphism is its Euler-characteristic trace. More precisely (Lemma B.1.2(2)), with 𝔻M = RHom(M, Λ[0]), TFAE: (a) M → 𝔻𝔻M and 𝔻M ⊗ M → 𝔻(M ⊗ 𝔻M) are isomorphisms; (b) M ⊗ 𝔻M → RHom(M, M) is an isomorphism; (c) M is strongly dualizable; (d) M is compact; (e) M is perfect.

items.name: The 2-category of correspondences of v-stacks
items.statement: For S decent, Corr_S has objects the decent S-v-stacks fine over S; 1-morphisms X → X' correspondences X ← C → X' with c_2 fine (then c_1 is fine), composed by fibre product; 2-morphisms c ⇒ d equivalence classes of proper p: C → D with 2-isomorphisms α_i: c_i ⇒ d_i∘p; symmetric monoidal by ×_S with unit S.

items.name: The 2-category of cohomological correspondences
items.statement: CoCorr_S has objects (X, A) with X ∈ Corr_S and A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ); 1-morphisms (c, u) with u: c_1^*A → c_2^!A', composed through the base-change map; 2-morphisms the proper (p, α_1, α_2) for which unit, α_1^*, u, α_2^! and counit compose to v (well defined on equivalence classes); ⊗ given by ×_S and ⊠_S with the Künneth map; iHom((X_1, A_1), (X_2, A_2)) = (X_1 ×_S X_2, RHom(pr_1^*A_1, pr_2^!A_2)).
items.note: See source issue E14 for a misprint in the tensor product.

items.name: Dualizability in CoCorr_S
items.statement: For X decent and fine over S and A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ), (X, A) is dualizable in CoCorr_S iff the natural map m: 𝔻_{X/S}A ⊠_S A → RHom(pr_1^*A, pr_2^!A) is an isomorphism; then the dual is (X, 𝔻_{X/S}A), with evaluation over (Δ_{X/S}, π) and coevaluation built from m^{-1}.

items.name: Dualizable means universally locally acyclic
items.statement: For f: X → S representable in nice diamonds, (X, A) is dualizable in CoCorr_S iff A is f-ULA (Fargues–Scholze IV.2.23–IV.2.24); this extends to fine maps of decent v-stacks because ULA is cohomologically-smooth-local on the source.
items.note: VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories VS1 plans ULA objects and FS IV.2 for representable maps; the extension to decent v-stacks is new.

items.name: Inertia stacks and characteristic classes
items.statement: For (X, A) dualizable and f = (c, u) ∈ End(X, A), tr(f) = (Fix(c), tr(u)) with Fix(c) = C ×_{X×_SX} X and tr(u) ∈ H^0(Fix(c), K_{Fix(c)/S}) the image of u under (P5), the dualizability isomorphism, evaluation and (BC2). For f = id, Fix = In_S(X), the inertia stack of pairs (x, g ∈ Aut x), and cc_{X/S}(A) := tr(id_A) ∈ H^0(In_S(X), K_{In_S(X)/S}) is the characteristic class.

items.name: Characteristic classes restrict to open substacks
items.statement: For i: U → X an open immersion of decent S-v-stacks fine over S, In_S(i) is an open immersion and, for A ULA over S, cc_{U/S}(i^*A) = In_S(i)^*cc_{X/S}(A).

items.name: Theorem 4.3.8: the relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula for v-stacks
items.statement: Let (X, A) be dualizable in CoCorr_S and f ∈ End(X, A) over c: C → X ×_S X, with proper maps q: X → X', p: C → C' compatible with a correspondence C' → X' ×_S X'. Then (X', q_*A) is dualizable, there is a unique f' ∈ End(X', q_*A) over C' such that p fills the square f'∘q ⇒ q∘f, and there is a (unique) 2-morphism tr(p̃): tr(f) ⇒ tr(f') over tr(p): tr(c) ⇒ tr(c').

items.name: Characteristic classes commute with proper pushforward
items.statement: For (X, A) dualizable and p: X → X' proper, (X', p_!A) is dualizable, In_S(p) is proper and In_S(p)_*cc_{X/S}(A) = cc_{X'/S}(p_!A).

items.name: The Lefschetz trace formula for proper diamonds
items.statement: For S = Spd C, q: X → S a nice proper diamond, A ULA over S and f = (c, u) over c: Y → X ×_S X, RΓ(X, A) is perfect and tr(q_*(f) | RΓ(X, A)) = ∫_{Fix(c)} ω for the trace class ω; if Fix(g) is finitely many isolated points, tr(g | RΓ(X, A)) = Σ_i loc_{x_i}(g, A).

items.name: Local terms
items.statement: For x ∈ Fix(c) isolated with x → S an isomorphism, loc_x(f) is the restriction of the trace class to x, in Λ; for f from an automorphism g with u: g^*A → A it is written loc_x(g, A). More generally loc_β(u, F) for a clopen β ⊆ Fix(c) proper over S is the image of tr_c(u, F) in H^0(S, Λ) (Section 5.3); local terms are additive in β.

items.name: Admissible objects on classifying stacks
items.statement: For G locally pro-p as above and M ∈ D_ét([S/G_S], Λ), TFAE: (1) ([S/G_S], M) is dualizable in CoCorr_S, with dual 𝔻M = Haar(G, Λ)^* ⊗ M^∨; (2) M is ULA over S; (3) M^K is a perfect complex for every compact open pro-p K ⊆ G. Such M are called admissible.

items.name: Trace distributions
items.statement: For M admissible, trdist(M) ∈ Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ Haar(G, Λ), Λ) sends h ⊗ μ to the Euler characteristic of I_{h,μ}(v) = ∫_G h(g)gv dμ(g), which factors through the perfect complex M^K for K small.

items.name: Characteristic class equals trace distribution
items.statement: In_S([S/G_S]) = [G_S//G_S] (the stack of conjugacy classes), H^0(In_S([S/G_S]), K) ≅ Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ Haar(G, Λ), Λ), and for M admissible cc_{[S/G_S]/S}(M) = trdist(M).

items.name: The modified Künneth map
items.statement: For U → T cohomologically smooth and fine f_i: Y_i → X_i over U → T (i = 1, 2), with f: Y_1 ×_U Y_2 → X_1 ×_T X_2 and g: Y_1 ×_U Y_2 → U, κ_{U/T}: f_1^!A_1 ⊠_U f_2^!A_2 → f^!(A_1 ⊠_T A_2) ⊗ g^*K_{U/T} is built from base change along Δ_{U/T} and Lemma 4.1.11; for X_i = T = S it is K_{Y_1/S} ⊠_U K_{Y_2/S} → K_{Y_1×_UY_2/S} ⊗ g^*K_{U/S}.

items.name: Inertia of a smooth base has canonically trivial dualizing complex
items.statement: If T is decent over S with π: T → S and Δ_{T/S} cohomologically smooth (e.g. T = [S/G] for G a cohomologically smooth locally spatial group diamond), then (T, Λ_T) is dualizable and cc_{T/S}(Λ_T): Λ_{In_S(T)} → K_{In_S(T)/S} is an isomorphism.

items.name: Theorem 4.5.3: a Künneth formula for characteristic classes
items.statement: Let T be decent over S with π and Δ_{T/S} cohomologically smooth, X_1, X_2 → T fine and A_i ∈ D_ét(X_i, Λ) ULA over S. Then A_1 ⊠_T A_2 is ULA over S and cc_{X_1/S}(A_1) ⊠_{In_S(T)} cc_{X_2/S}(A_2) = cc_{X_1×_TX_2/S}(A_1 ⊠_T A_2), using In_S(X_1 ×_T X_2) ≅ In_S(X_1) ×_{In_S(T)} In_S(X_2) and Lemma 4.5.2.

items.name: Based cohomological correspondences and fibre products over a base
items.statement: BCoCorr_S has objects (X → T, A, B) with T → S cohomologically smooth and B ∈ D_ét(T, Λ) invertible; morphisms (q^♮, α, β) with q^♮ a morphism of based correspondences whose base map u' is cohomologically smooth, α: c^*A → c'^!A' and β: u^*B ≅ u'^!B'; with functors 𝓑 (base) and 𝓢 (source) to CoCorr_S and the monoidal fibre-product functor 𝔛_1 ⊠_𝔗 𝔛_2 = (X_1 ×_T X_2, (A_1 ⊠_T A_2) ⊗ p^*B^{-1}, B), functorial and monoidal up to coherent 2-isomorphism.
items.note: The paper states that the functoriality and monoidality 2-isomorphisms are 'straightforward but tedious' and omits them; the design job must supply them.

items.name: Theorem 4.6.1: characteristic classes on [X/G] are universal local terms
items.statement: Let X be a nice diamond over S with an action of a cohomologically smooth S-group diamond G, Y = [X/G], A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) ULA over S, X_G = X ×_S G and (c̃, ũ) the endomorphism of (X_G, A|_{X_G}) in CoCorr_G given by (x, g) ↦ (g(x), g). With ι: H^0(In_S(Y), K_{In_S(Y)/S}) → H^0(Fix(c̃), K_{Fix(c̃)/G}) built from the cartesian square Fix(c̃) → G over In_S(Y) → [G//G] and Lemma 4.5.2, ι(cc_{Y/S}(A)) = tr_{c̃}(ũ, A|_{X_G}); the latter restricts at g ∈ G(S) to tr(g, u_g).

items.name: On the locus of isolated fixed points the characteristic class is the local-term function
items.statement: If U ⊆ G is conjugation-invariant open and its elements have only isolated fixed points on X, then In_S([X/G])_U → [U//G] is étale, K is canonically trivial there, and cc_{[X/G]/S}(A)_U is the function (x, g) ↦ loc_x(g, A) on pairs with g(x) = x.

items.name: The Lefschetz–Verdier formalism for schemes
items.statement: For a separated finite-type X over an algebraically closed k and A constructible of bounded amplitude, 𝔻A ⊠^L_k A ≅ RHom(pr_1^*A, pr_2^!A) (SGA 5 III (3.1.1)); cohomological correspondences have trace classes on fixed-point schemes compatible with proper pushforward (Lu–Zheng; Varshavsky), with local terms at isolated fixed points.

items.name: Local terms commute with base change
items.statement: For f: X → S representable in nice diamonds, a correspondence c over S with c_1 proper and a clopen β ⊆ Fix(c) proper over S, an f-ULA F with cohomological correspondence u, and any a: T → S, the map H^0(S, Λ) → H^0(T, Λ) sends loc_β(u, F) to loc_{β_T}(u_T, F_T); for S, T connected they are equal.

items.name: Perfect schemes and v-sheaves: the comparison of local terms
items.statement: For k perfect, the functor X ↦ X^♢ from perfect schemes over k commutes with finite limits, sends separated perfectly finite type maps to maps representable in locally spatial diamonds, compactifiable of finite dim.trg, and c_X^*: D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(X^♢, Λ) is fully faithful symmetric monoidal, compatible with f^* and Rf_!, with maps c_X^*RHom → RHom and c_X^*Rf^! → Rf^{♢!}c_Y^* (ECD §27).

items.name: Local terms of perfect schemes agree with those of their v-sheaves
items.statement: For X separated and perfectly of finite type over k, a correspondence c with c_1 and f∘c' perfectly proper, an f-ULA F with cohomological correspondence u and β ⊆ Fix(c) clopen, c_X^*F is f^♢-ULA and loc_β(u, F) = loc_{β^♢}(u^♢, c_X^*F).

items.name: Double duals of modules over R/𝔪^k
items.statement: For R a discrete valuation ring and Λ = R/𝔪^k, a Λ-module M satisfies M ≅ M^{**} iff M is finitely generated; consequently M → 𝔻𝔻M in D(Λ) is an isomorphism iff every H^i(M) is finitely generated (Λ is self-injective).
items.locator: Lemma B.1.1, p. 72; and Lemma B.1.2(1), p. 73
items.note: See source issue E12 for misprints in the proof.

items.name: Smooth and complete modules over functions on a locally profinite set
items.statement: For S locally profinite and Λ discrete, a C(S, Λ)-module M is smooth if M ⊗_{C(S,Λ)} C_c(S, Λ) ≅ M (equivalently colim_U 1_U M ≅ M) and complete if M ≅ lim_U 1_U M, U over compact opens; M ↦ M^s and M ↦ M^c are projectors giving inverse equivalences between smooth and complete modules.
items.locator: Definition B.2.1, p. 74; Lemmas B.2.2–B.2.3, p. 74

items.name: Sheaves on a locally profinite set are smooth modules
items.statement: For R(U) = C(U, Λ), restriction F(S) → F(U) is surjective with 1_U F(S) ≅ F(U) and F(S) = lim_U F(U); M ↦ F_M, F ↦ M^s_F (resp. M^c_F) give inverse equivalences between smooth (resp. complete) C(S, Λ)-modules and R-module sheaves on S, with F_M(S) = M^c.
items.locator: Lemma B.2.5, p. 74; and Lemma B.2.4, p. 74

items.name: The B_dR^+-affine Grassmannian, Schubert cells, the local Hecke stack and the Satake category
items.statement: Over Spd C, Gr_G = LG/L^+G (LG(R) = G(B_dR(R)), L^+G(R) = G(B_dR^+(R))) is an ind-spatial diamond with L^+G-action, the closed Schubert cells Gr_{G,≤μ} are proper, Hecke^loc_G = [L^+G\Gr_G], and Sat_G(Λ) ⊆ D_ét(Hecke^loc_{G,C}, Λ) (Λ = Z/ℓ^n[√q] or Z_ℓ[√q]) is the full subcategory of perverse, Λ-flat, ULA objects (Fargues–Scholze I.6.2), symmetric monoidal under convolution; the L^+G-action on Gr_{G,≤μ} factors through a truncation L^+_mG.

items.name: Geometric Satake (Fargues–Scholze)
items.statement: There is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal categories Rep_Ĝ(Λ) ≅ Sat_G(Λ), V ↦ S_V, with Rep_Ĝ(Λ) the representations of the dual group on finite projective Λ-modules (Fargues–Scholze, Theorem I.6.3).

items.name: Fixed points of strongly regular elements on affine Grassmannians
items.statement: Let K^+ be a discrete valuation ring with algebraically closed residue field k and fraction field K, G reductive over K^+, g ∈ G(K^+) with strongly regular image in G(k), T = Cent(g, G). Then T(K)/T(K^+) ≅ (G(K)/G(K^+))^g, so the fixed points are X_*(T); for any incarnation of the affine Grassmannian, Gr^g_{G,≤μ} is finite over the base with underlying set X_*(T)_{≤μ} (proof through the Bruhat–Tits building of G_K and its hyperspecial vertex).

items.name: Theorem 5.1.3: local terms of Satake sheaves at fixed points
items.statement: For V ∈ Rep(Ĝ), g ∈ G(F)_sr and x ∈ Gr_G^g with ν_x ∈ X^*_+(T̂) the open Schubert cell containing x, loc_x(g, S_V) = (−1)^{⟨2ρ, ν_x⟩} rank_Λ V[ν_x].

items.name: The characteristic class of a Satake sheaf on the local Hecke stack
items.statement: If S_V is supported on Gr_{G,≤μ} and L^+G acts on it through L^+_mG, with X = [Gr_{G,≤μ}/L^+_mG], the connected components of In_S(X)_sr are X_*^+(T)_{≤μ}/W, its dualizing complex is canonically trivial, and cc_{X/S}(S_V) restricted to In_S(X)_sr is λ ↦ (−1)^{⟨2ρ_G, λ⟩} rank_Λ V[λ].

items.name: Local terms depend only on the Schubert cell
items.statement: For g, g' ∈ G(F)_sr and fixed points x ∈ Gr_G^g, x' ∈ Gr_G^{g'} with ν_x = ν_{x'}, loc_x(g, S_V) = loc_{x'}(g', S_V).

items.name: Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian from B_dR to Witt vectors, with compatible Satake
items.statement: For a split reductive model 𝒢/O_F, the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian Gr_𝒢 over Spd O_C has generic fibre Gr_G and special fibre (Gr^W_𝒢)^♢ (cartesian squares), and the Satake functors on the three are compatible, the restrictions being equivalences on the essential images of Rep(Ĝ).

items.name: Fixed points on the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian
items.statement: For g ∈ 𝒢(O_F) with strongly regular semisimple reduction, 𝒯 = Cent(g, 𝒢) is a maximal torus and Gr_𝒢^g ≅ Gr_𝒯 ≅ X_*(𝒯)_S (Scholze–Weinstein 21.3.1, 20.3.7); each component β ≃ S gives isolated fixed points β_η, β_s in the two fibres.

items.name: Local terms are constant from characteristic 0 to characteristic p
items.statement: For g as above, V ∈ Rep(Ĝ) and a component β ⊆ Gr_𝒢^g, loc_{β_η}(g, j^*S_V) = loc_{β_s}(g, i^*S_V).

items.name: Local terms on the Witt vector affine Grassmannian
items.statement: For g ∈ 𝒢(O_F) of finite prime-to-p order with strongly regular semisimple reduction, x ∈ Gr^{W,g}_𝒢 and V ∈ Rep(Ĝ), loc_x(g, S_V) = (−1)^{⟨2ρ, ν_x⟩} rank_Λ V[ν_x].

items.name: Inertia of truncated positive loop group quotients over the strongly regular locus
items.statement: (1) [L^+_mG_sr//L^+_mG] ≅ [L^+_mT_sr/(W ⋉ L^+_mT)]. (2) In_S([Gr_{G,≤μ}/L^+_mG])_sr ≅ X_*(T)_{≤μ} ×^W [L^+_mT_sr//L^+_mT], compatibly with the projections; hence H^0(In_S(X)_sr, K) ≅ C(X_*(T)_{≤μ}, Λ)^W, sending cc_{X/S}(S_V) to λ ↦ loc_{x_λ}(g, S_V) for any g ∈ L^+_mT_sr, which is independent of g.

items.name: Perfect projectivity of Witt vector Schubert varieties
items.statement: Finite unions of closed Schubert cells of the Witt vector affine Grassmannian are perfectly projective k-schemes (Bhatt–Scholze).

items.name: Euler characteristics of semi-infinite orbits
items.statement: For X a finite union of closed Witt Schubert cells containing supp S_V and X_ν = X ∩ S_ν (S_ν the semi-infinite orbit), H^d_c(X_ν, S_V) vanishes unless d = ⟨2ρ, ν⟩, where it is the ν-weight functor (Yu, integral geometric Satake, Proposition 4.2); hence χ_c(X_ν, S_V) = (−1)^{⟨2ρ,ν⟩} rank V[ν].
items.note: GS1 plans semi-infinite orbits and the integral special/generic-fibre comparison, GS4 the weight functors; Yu's integral Witt-vector statement is the input they must supply.

items.name: Varshavsky: true and naive local terms agree for finite-order automorphisms
items.statement: For X of finite type over an algebraically closed k of characteristic p, g an automorphism of finite prime-to-p order and A ∈ D^b_c(X, Z_ℓ) with u: g^*A → A, loc_x(g, A) = tr(g | A_x) at every isolated fixed point x (Varshavsky, local terms, Theorem 4.10(b) and Corollary 5.4(b)).

items.name: True and naive local terms agree on perfect schemes
items.statement: For X perfectly of finite type over an algebraically closed k, g of finite prime-to-p order and A ∈ D^b_c(X, Z_ℓ) with u: g^*A → A, loc_x(g, A) = tr(g | A_x) at isolated fixed points; in particular loc_x(g, A) = loc_x(g, A|_Z) for g-stable closed Z (reduce to a g-stable finite-type deperfection and apply Varshavsky).

items.name: Bun_G and its strata
items.statement: Bun_G is a cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack over Spd k; Bun_G^b ≅ [Spd k/G̃_b] with 0 → G̃_b^∘ → G̃_b → G_b(F) → 0, G̃_b^∘ cohomologically smooth; for b basic i_b is an open immersion and G̃_b = G_b(F) (Fargues–Scholze III).

items.name: Global and local Hecke stacks
items.statement: The Hecke stack Hecke_{G,C} of (E_1, E_2, f) with f an isomorphism off D_T meromorphic along D_T, its local version Hecke^loc_{G,C} ≅ [L^+G\LG/L^+G] over Bun^loc_{G,C} ≅ [Spd C/L^+G], the maps h_1, h_2 and completion maps form a diagram with cartesian squares (Beauville–Laszlo gluing); bounded versions Hecke_{G,≤μ,C}.

items.name: Decency of Bun_G, bounded Hecke stacks and truncated local Hecke stacks
items.statement: Bun_{G,C} is a decent v-stack fine over Spd C; Hecke_{G,≤μ,C} is decent with h_1, h_2 fine; [Gr_{G,≤μ,C}/L^+_mG] (but not [Gr_{G,≤μ,C}/L^+G]) is a decent S-v-stack with fine structure map.

items.name: Local shtuka spaces as fibres of the Hecke stack, and the two period maps
items.statement: For b ∈ B(G, μ) basic, the open substacks Hecke^{b,1}, Hecke^{∗,1}, Hecke^{b,∗} of Hecke_{G,≤μ,C} over Bun^b, Bun^1 fit into a diagram of cartesian squares (6.1.2) with Hecke^{∗,1} ≅ [Gr^1_{G,≤μ}/G(F)], Hecke^{b,1} ≅ [Gr^{1,adm}_{G,≤μ}/G(F)] ≅ [Gr^{b,adm}_{G,≤μ}/G_b(F)] and Gr^b_{G,≤μ} ≅ Gr_{G,≤−μ}; Sht_{G,b,μ,C} = Hecke^{b,1} ×_{Bun^b×Bun^1} Spd C; and π_1: Sht → Gr^b_{G,≤μ}, π_2: Sht → Gr^1_{G,≤μ} are respectively a G(F)-torsor and a G_b(F)-torsor over the admissible loci, equivariantly for the other group.

items.name: The Kottwitz invariant of a modification by a cocharacter
items.statement: For E a G-bundle on X_C trivialized at ∞, T ⊆ G a maximal torus, λ ∈ X_*(T) with character λ̂ of T̂ and E[λ] the modification by the T-fixed lattice L_λ, κ(E[λ]) = κ(E) + λ̂|_{Z(Ĝ)^Γ} in X^*(Z(Ĝ)^Γ) (Caraiani–Scholze Lemma 3.5.5, with the opposite Schubert-cell convention).

items.name: Fixed points of pairs on local shtuka spaces
items.statement: If (g, g') ∈ G(F)_sr × G_b(F)_sr fixes x ∈ Sht_{G,b,μ}(C), with T = Cent(g, G), T' = Cent(g', G_b), then π_1(x) and π_2(x) correspond to λ' ∈ X_*(T')_{≤−μ} and λ ∈ X_*(T)_{≤μ}; there is y ∈ G(F̆) with Ad y an F-rational isomorphism T → T' carrying g to g' and λ to −λ'; and inv[b](g, g') is the image of λ in X_*(T)_Γ ≅ B(T), so (g, g', λ) ∈ Rel_{b,μ}.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.3: elliptic fixed points are admissible
items.statement: For g ∈ G(F)_ell, every fixed point of g on Gr^1_{G,≤μ} lies in the admissible locus Gr^{1,adm}_{G,≤μ}; for g' ∈ G_b(F)_ell, every fixed point of g' on Gr^b_{G,≤−μ} lies in Gr^{b,adm}_{G,≤−μ}.
items.note: Proof: E^1[λ] ≅ E^{b'} with g transported to an automorphism of E^{b'} whose image in G_{b'}(F) is conjugate to g, so G_{b'} contains a torus elliptic in G; elliptic tori transfer across inner forms (Kottwitz 1986 §10), forcing b' basic, and κ(b') = κ(b).

items.name: Elliptic maximal tori transfer across inner forms
items.statement: An elliptic maximal torus of G transfers to every inner form; if an inner form of a Levi M^* of G^* contains a maximal torus elliptic for G^*, then M^* = G^* (Kottwitz 1986 §10).

items.name: The elliptic inertia of the Hecke stack is the relation space
items.statement: The elliptic parts of In_S(Hecke^{b,∗}), In_S(Hecke^{∗,1}) and In_S(Hecke^{b,1}) coincide, and |In_S(Hecke^{b,1}_{G,≤μ,S})_ell| ≅ Rel_{b,μ,ell}.

items.name: Integration along torsors of locally profinite sets
items.statement: For H locally pro-p with a Λ-valued Haar measure (p ∈ Λ^×) and h: T̃ → T an H-torsor of locally profinite sets, integration along fibres gives isomorphisms of C(T, Λ)-modules C_c(T̃, Λ)_H ≅ C_c(T, Λ) and Dist(T̃, Λ)^H ≅ Dist(T, Λ).

items.name: The geometric transfer on elliptic coinvariants
items.statement: With the elliptic fixed-point loci Fix(α_b)_ell ← Fix(α_Sht)_ell → Fix(α_1)_ell (p_1 a G_b(F)-equivariant G(F)-torsor, p_2 a G(F)-equivariant G_b(F)-torsor, q_1, q_2 finite étale over the elliptic loci), T̃^{G→G_b}_{b,μ}: C_c(G(F)_ell, Λ)_{G(F)} → C_c(G_b(F)_ell, Λ)_{G_b(F)} is q_{1*}∘(·K_μ)∘(p_1)_*∘(p_2)_*^{-1}∘q_2^*, with K_μ(g', λ') = (−1)^d rank V_μ^∨[λ'].

items.name: The geometric transfer computes the Hecke transfer of orbital integrals
items.statement: For Λ = Q̄_ℓ, φ ∈ C_c(G(F)_ell, Λ) and φ' ∈ C_c(G_b(F)_ell, Λ) any lift of T̃^{G→G_b}_{b,μ}φ, φ'_{G_b} = T^{G→G_b}_{b,μ}φ_G.
items.note: See source issue E10 for a misprint in the proof.

items.name: Transfer of invariant distributions
items.statement: 𝒯^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}: Dist(G_b(F)_ell, Λ)^{G_b(F)} → Dist(G(F)_ell, Λ)^{G(F)} is the Λ-linear dual of T̃^{G→G_b}_{b,μ}.

items.name: The distribution transfer extends the function transfer
items.statement: For Λ = Q̄_ℓ and f ∈ C(G_b(F)_ell, Λ)^{G_b(F)}, 𝒯^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}(f dg') = T^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}(f) dg (by the Weyl integration formula, Lemma 3.4.1 and Proposition 6.3.3).

items.name: Sheaves on basic strata and ULA objects on Bun_G
items.statement: D(G_b(F), Λ) ≅ D_lis(Bun_G^b, Λ) (Fargues–Scholze I.5.1); A ∈ D_lis(Bun_G, Λ) is ULA over Spd k iff every i_b^*A is admissible (perfect K-invariants for pro-p K ⊆ G_b(F)), and ULA objects are stable under Verdier duality with biduality (FS I.5.1(v)).

items.name: Extension by zero and pushforward of admissible representations are ULA
items.statement: For b ∈ B(G) and ρ an admissible complex in D(G_b(F), Λ), (i_b)_!ρ and (i_b)_*ρ are ULA over Spd k (the latter by Verdier duality 𝔻((i_b)_!ρ^∨) ≅ (i_b)_*ρ).

items.name: Hecke operators and their properties (Fargues–Scholze)
items.statement: For V ∈ Rep_Ĝ(Λ), T_V(F) = h_{2!}(h_1^*F ⊗ S_V) on D_lis(Bun_{G,C}, Λ); Hecke operators preserve ULA and compact objects, T_V has left and right adjoint T_{V^∨}, and they are compatible with extension of scalars (Fargues–Scholze IX.0.1).

items.name: Cohomology of local shtuka spaces as a Hecke operator
items.statement: For K ⊆ G(F) compact open and I_{K,Λ} = cInd_K^{G(F)}Λ, RΓ_c(Sht_{G,b,μ,K,C}, S_{μ,Λ}) ≅ i_b^*T_{V_{μ,Λ}}(i_1)_!I_{K,Λ} in D(G_b(F), Λ); consequently RΓ(G, b, μ)[ρ] ≅ i_1^*T_{V_μ^∨}(i_b)_*ρ, admissible (resp. of finite length) when ρ is (Fargues–Scholze IX.3.2, I.7.3).

items.name: RΓ(G, b, μ)[−] for general coefficients
items.statement: For any Z_ℓ-algebra Λ, RΓ(G, b, μ)[−] := i_1^*T_{V^∨_{μ,Λ}}(i_b)_*(−): D(G_b(F), Λ) → D(G(F), Λ), compatible with scalar extension, preserving admissibility, and preserving finite length for Λ Artinian.

items.name: The trace distribution of shtuka cohomology on the elliptic locus
items.statement: For Λ a torsion Z_ℓ-algebra, compatible Z_ℓ-valued Haar measures on G(F), G_b(F) and ρ an admissible Λ-representation of G_b(F), trdist(RΓ(G, b, μ)[ρ])_ell = 𝒯^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}(trdist(ρ)_ell) in Dist(G(F)_ell, Λ)^{G(F)}.
items.note: Proof: characteristic classes on Bun^1 (Lemma 4.3.7, Corollary 4.3.9 for the proper h_2, Corollary 6.2.4), the fibre product H^{b,∗} = B^b ×_{B^loc_m} H^loc_m and Theorem 4.5.3, then Proposition 6.4.8.

items.name: The characteristic class of ρ ⊠ S_{V^∨} on the strongly regular locus
items.statement: cc(ρ ⊠ S_{V^∨})_sr ∈ H^0(In_S(H^{b,∗})_sr, K) ≅ Dist(Fix(α_b)_sr, Λ)^{G_b(F)} is the image of trdist(ρ) ⊗ (−1)^{⟨2ρ_G,−⟩}rank V^∨[−] under Dist(G_b(F)_sr, Λ)^{G_b(F)} ⊗ C(X_*(T)_{≤−μ}, Λ)^W → Dist(Fix(α_b)_sr, Λ)^{G_b(F)}.

items.name: The character identity for representations with a lattice
items.statement: For ρ a finite-length admissible Q̄_ℓ-representation of G_b(F) admitting a Z̄_ℓ-lattice and φ ∈ C_c(G(F)_ell, Q̄_ℓ), tr(φ | Mant_{b,μ}(ρ)) = [𝒯^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}(trdist ρ)](φ).

items.name: The character identity in general
items.statement: For every finite-length admissible Q̄_ℓ-representation ρ of G_b(F) and φ ∈ C_c(G(F)_ell, Q̄_ℓ), tr(φ | Mant_{b,μ}(ρ)) = [𝒯^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}(trdist ρ)](φ); hence the virtual character of Mant_{b,μ}(ρ) on G(F)_ell equals T^{G_b→G}_{b,μ}(Θ_ρ).

items.name: Mant_{b,μ} is continuous: its traces are trace forms
items.statement: For φ ∈ C_c(G(F), Q̄_ℓ) and w ∈ W_E, the linear form ρ ↦ tr(φ × w | RΓ(G, b, μ)[ρ]) on Groth(G_b(F)) is a trace form (the trace of some function in C_c(G_b(F), Q̄_ℓ)); in particular tr(φ | Mant_{b,μ}(−)) is a trace form. (Conjectured by Taylor for Rapoport–Zink spaces; proved by checking the two conditions of the trace Paley–Wiener theorem.)

items.name: Endoscopic data attached to a parameter and z-pairs
items.statement: For a discrete φ and semisimple s ∈ S_φ with lift ṡ ∈ S_φ^+, Ĥ = Cent(s, Ĝ)^∘, ℋ = Ĥ·φ(W_F) and the quasi-split H dual to Ĥ (Galois action through Out(Ĥ)) give a refined elliptic endoscopic datum (H, ℋ, ṡ, η); a z-pair (H_1, η_1) exists (Kottwitz–Shelstad §2.2), giving φ^s = η_1∘φ and SΘ_{φ^s} = Σ_{π^s} dim(τ_{π^s})Θ_{π^s}.
items.note: ET.0 plans endoscopic triples, z-extensions and endoscopic groups; the refined datum with ṡ ∈ S_φ^+ is part of Kaletha's framework (item 009).

items.name: The endoscopic character identities as functions
items.statement: Assuming Conjecture G, for strongly regular g ∈ G(F): e(G)Σ_{π∈Π_φ(G)} tr τ_{z,𝔴,π}(ṡ)Θ_π(g) = Σ_{h_1∈H_1(F)/st} Δ(h_1, g)SΘ_{φ^s}(h_1), and likewise for G_{z_b} and g' ∈ G_{z_b}(F), with Δ = Δ'_abs the Langlands–Shelstad transfer factors of Kaletha's rigid setting.

items.name: Transfer factors of G and G_b differ by the isocrystal invariant
items.statement: Δ(h_1, g') = Δ(h_1, g)·⟨inv[b](g, g'), s^♮_{h,g}⟩, where s^♮ is the image of ṡ in S_φ, transported by the admissible isomorphism φ_{h,g} into T̂_g^Γ and paired with inv[b](g, g') via B(T_g) ≅ X^*(T̂_g^Γ) (from Kaletha's rigid transfer factors and ⟨inv[b], s^♮⟩ = ⟨inv[z_b], ṡ⟩, Kaletha 2018 §4.2).

items.name: The Kottwitz sign through the dual group
items.statement: If the inner twist ψ: G^* → G has class h ∈ H^1(Γ, G^*_ad) corresponding to ν ∈ X^*(Z(Ĝ_sc)^Γ) (Kottwitz 1986, Theorem 1.2) and 2ρ is the sum of the positive coroots of Ĝ_sc, then e(G) = (−1)^{⟨2ρ, ν⟩} (well defined mod 2).

items.name: Non-elliptic virtual representations are combinations of parabolic inductions
items.statement: A finite-length virtual G(F)-representation with C- or Q̄_ℓ-coefficients is non-elliptic iff it is a Q-linear combination of representations induced from proper parabolic subgroups (parabolic inductions are non-elliptic by van Dijk's formula; the converse from Dat's results on K_0: π = Σ_{d(M)>d(G)} c_d(M) i_M^G r_G^M(π)).
items.note: For G(F) with compact centre this is a weaker form of Kazhdan's theorem.

items.name: Z̄_ℓ-lattices in admissible representations
items.statement: An admissible smooth Q̄_ℓ-representation π admits a Z̄_ℓ-lattice if there is an admissible smooth ℓ-torsion-free Z̄_ℓ[G(F)]-module L with L[1/ℓ] ≅ π; then each L^K is finite free and, for π of finite length, L is finitely generated (Vignéras).

items.name: Standard modules of lattice-admitting representations generate the Grothendieck group
items.statement: Groth(G(F)) is generated by i_M^G(σ ⊗ ψ) with M a standard Levi, ψ an unramified character and σ an irreducible admissible Q̄_ℓ-representation of M(F) admitting a Z̄_ℓ-lattice; indeed the standard representations I(π), π with cuspidal support θ, form a basis of Groth(G(F))_θ.

items.name: ν-tempered irreducible representations admit lattices
items.statement: Every irreducible smooth Q̄_ℓ-representation of G(F) that is ν-tempered (Dat) admits a Z̄_ℓ-lattice.

items.name: Langlands data decrease along the standard module
items.statement: Write π = j_P^G(σ ⊗ ψ) (Dat's ℓ-adic Langlands classification, λ_π = −ν(ψ)); for π' a subquotient of I(π) = i_M^G(σ ⊗ ψ), λ_{π'} ≤ λ_π, with strict inequality if π' is a subquotient of ker(I(π) → π). More precisely, exponents μ' of any subquotient of i_P^G(σ ⊗ ψ) satisfy μ' ≤ μ = −ν(ψ), strictly on the kernel of the Langlands quotient.
items.locator: Lemma C.2.4, p. 76; Proposition C.2.5, p. 76

items.name: Representations with lattices are dense
items.statement: The irreducible π ∈ Irr_{Q̄_ℓ}(G(F)) admitting Z̄_ℓ-lattices are dense: a trace form on Groth(G(F)) vanishing on them vanishes identically (integral unramified characters, and those with i_M^G(σψ) irreducible, are Zariski dense; Dat Theorem 5.1).

items.name: The trace Paley–Wiener theorem (Bernstein–Deligne–Kazhdan)
items.statement: A linear form f on Groth(H(F)) is a trace form tr(φ | −), φ ∈ C_c(H(F), Q̄_ℓ), iff (1) for some compact open K, f(π) ≠ 0 only if π^K ≠ 0, and (2) for every parabolic P = MU and irreducible σ of M(F), ψ ↦ f(i_M^H(σψ)) is algebraic in the unramified character ψ.

routes.title: Hecke correspondences and local shtuka cohomology, Part II: the Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula and the Kottwitz conjecture
routes.brief:
Extend Hecke correspondences and local shtuka cohomology (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas), starting where it stops: HS0–HS3 construct Hecke stacks, the Hecke action, local shtuka moduli and their cohomology as a representation-valued functor, but compute nothing about that cohomology. This Part II computes it on the elliptic locus, following Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein, On the Kottwitz conjecture for local shtuka spaces (Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e13). Final theorems, as stated there:

Theorem 1.0.2. Assume the refined local Langlands correspondence (Kaletha, Conjecture G). Let φ: W_F × SL_2 → ^LG be a discrete L-parameter with Q̄_ℓ-coefficients and ρ ∈ Π_φ(G_b), b the basic class of B(G, μ). After ignoring the W_E-action, Mant_{b,μ}(ρ) = Σ_{π∈Π_φ(G)} dim Hom_{S_φ}(δ_{π,ρ}, r_μ)·π + err in Groth(G(F)), with err a virtual representation whose character vanishes on the elliptic locus; if Π_φ(G) is supercuspidal and the Fargues–Scholze parameter φ_ρ is supercuspidal, err = 0.

Theorem 1.0.3. For G an inner form of GL_n/F and π irreducible smooth, the Fargues–Scholze parameter φ_π is the usual semisimplified L-parameter.

Also export Theorem 3.2.9 (the endoscopic trace relation for the Hecke transfer maps), Theorem 5.1.3 (local terms of Satake sheaves at fixed points: (−1)^{⟨2ρ,ν_x⟩} rank V[ν_x]), Theorem 6.2.3 (elliptic fixed points are admissible), Proposition 6.4.7 and Theorem 6.5.2 (the trace distribution of shtuka cohomology on the elliptic locus is the transfer of trdist ρ), and Theorem 6.5.4 (tr(φ × w | RΓ(G, b, μ)[−]) is a trace form, Taylor's conjecture for Rapoport–Zink spaces).

Coverage, in order. (1) The objects of the conjecture: rigid inner forms, Kottwitz's gerbe description of B(G), the refined LLC (Conjecture G) as an explicit hypothesis, S_φ^+, δ_{π,ρ} and its independence (Section 2); if the Kaletha extraction's proposed Part II of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison (rigid inner forms) is accepted, import these from it instead. (2) Hecke transfer maps: Rel_b, T_{b,μ}, Theorem 3.2.9 with the sign identity, adjointness (Section 3 and Appendix A.1). (3) Fixed points and local terms on the B_dR^+-, Beilinson–Drinfeld and Witt Grassmannians (Section 5 except 5.3). (4) Hecke stacks as decent v-stacks, shtuka spaces as their fibres, fixed points and elliptic admissibility, inertia (Sections 6.1–6.2). (5) The distribution transfer (Section 6.3). (6) The trace distribution of RΓ(G, b, μ)[ρ], the lattice and general cases, the trace-form theorem (Sections 6.4–6.5). (7) Theorems 1.0.2 and 1.0.3 (Sections 6.5–6.6).

Imports: HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS0–HS3 (parent); the proposed Part II of VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories (decent v-stacks and the Lefschetz–Verdier formalism) and the proposed Part II of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (characters, trace Paley–Wiener, lattices) from this extraction; VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories VS4–VS5; GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0–GS4; ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES5, ES6 and ES7:GLn-comparison (the GL_n case of Theorem 1.0.3); EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.0, ET.1 and ET.6 (stable conjugacy, transfer factors, Jacquet–Langlands); BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0–BG3; ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 (buildings); EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.8 (scheme local terms, with Varshavsky's theorem added there).

Tests: the Lubin–Tate case (GL_n, μ = (1, 0, …, 0), b of slope 1/n: Mant = nπ + err, recovering Faltings, Strauch and Mieda); Example 3.2.10 (GL_2, the Jacquet–Langlands identity Θ_ρ(g') = −Θ_π(g)); the GSp(4) and U(1, n−1) basic Rapoport–Zink cases (Mieda, Shen); a non-minuscule μ; and the multi-leg extension the paper leaves to the reader (cohomology over (Div^1)^I).
routes.reason: The paper computes the cohomology of the local shtuka spaces that HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas constructs (HS2) and turns into a representation-valued functor (HS3); that is the direction of HS, which stops before any computation. Its new mathematics (Hecke transfer, local terms of Satake sheaves, fixed points on Hecke stacks, the distribution transfer, the Kottwitz conjecture, inner forms of GL_n) extends that roadmap. The general trace formalism and the representation-theoretic tools go to their own owners (routes 2 and 3).

routes.title: Artin v-stacks, solid and lisse coefficient categories, Part II: decent v-stacks, cohomological correspondences and the Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula
routes.brief:
Extend Artin v-stacks, solid and lisse coefficient categories (VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories), starting where VS0–VS1 stop (Artin v-stacks, partial compact-support functors, ULA objects): construct Gulotta–Hansen–Weinstein's decent v-stacks and fine morphisms with genuine !-functors for stacky maps, and the Lefschetz–Verdier trace formalism of Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein §4 and §5.3 (Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e13), following Lu–Zheng's categorical traces. Final theorems, as stated there:

Theorem 4.1.8 (GHW). For any fine map f of decent v-stacks there are Rf_!, Rf^! satisfying the projection formula, local Verdier duality, (P5) and base change, agreeing with Scholze's for maps representable in nice diamonds, pseudo-functorial, with Rf_! ≅ Rf_* for proper f, and cohomological smoothness with smooth base change.

Theorem 4.3.8 (relative Lefschetz–Verdier). For (X, A) dualizable in CoCorr_S and f ∈ End(X, A) over C → X ×_S X, with proper q: X → X', p: C → C' compatible with C' → X' ×_S X', (X', q_*A) is dualizable, there is a unique f' over C' filled by p, and a 2-morphism tr(f) ⇒ tr(f') over tr(p). Corollary 4.3.9: In_S(p)_*cc_{X/S}(A) = cc_{X'/S}(p_!A).

Also: Proposition 4.3.5 and the equivalence dualizable ⇔ ULA for fine maps; Proposition 4.4.1 and 4.4.3 (admissible objects on [S/G_S], cc = trdist); Theorem 4.5.3 (Künneth for characteristic classes over a base with smooth diagonal, via BCoCorr_S); Theorem 4.6.1 (cc on [X/G] is the universal local term); Propositions 5.3.1–5.3.2 (local terms commute with base change and with passage from perfect schemes to v-sheaves); Examples 4.2.1–4.2.5 (locally profinite sets, classifying stacks, Haar measures); Lemmas B.1.1–B.1.2 (dualizable = perfect in D(Λ)) and B.2.1–B.2.5 (sheaves on locally profinite sets). The functoriality and monoidality of ⊠ over a base (4.5.7–4.5.8), which the paper calls 'straightforward but tedious', must be proved.

The Abe extraction's proposed Part II of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheavesPartIIRelativeTraces) plans the same generic 2-categorical trace interface for schemes, after Lu–Zheng; the two continuations should share one home for it rather than duplicate it. routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: characters, trace Paley–Wiener and ℓ-adic lattices
routes.brief: Extend Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups), starting where SR.0–SR.3 stop (smooth categories, Hecke algebras, induction and Jacquet functors, admissibility): add the character theory and ℓ-adic tools that Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein (Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e13) use for connected reductive G over a p-adic field F. Final theorems: (1) Harish-Chandra's theorem that the trace distribution of a finite-length admissible representation is given on G(F)_sr by a locally constant character Θ_π; (2) G(F)_rs//G(F) is locally profinite, a disjoint union of T(F)_rs/N(T, G)(F) (Lemma 3.1.1); (3) compatible Haar measures on inner forms and related tori, the orbital-integral isomorphism C_c(G(F)_sr, Λ)_{G(F)} ≅ C_c(G(F)_sr//G(F), Λ) and the stable Weyl integration formula (§3.4); (4) the trace Paley–Wiener theorem of Bernstein–Deligne–Kazhdan; (5) Theorem C.1.1: a finite-length virtual representation is non-elliptic iff it is a Q-linear combination of proper parabolic inductions (van Dijk; Dat, On the K_0 of a p-adic group); (6) Dat's ℓ-adic Langlands classification and ν-tempered representations: ν-tempered irreducibles admit Z̄_ℓ-lattices (Lemma C.2.3), the exponent inequalities of Lemma C.2.4 and Proposition C.2.5, standard modules of lattice-admitting representations generate Groth(G(F)) (Proposition C.2.2), and representations with lattices are dense for trace forms (Lemma 6.5.5). Imports: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0–SR.3 and SR.6 (parent); EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.0–ET.1 (stable conjugacy, orbital integrals); ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0 (topology of G(F)); the Tau Ceti Lie groups roadmap's Weyl integration (Layer 6) as the real model. Tests: GL_2 (principal series non-elliptic, Steinberg and supercuspidals), SL_2, the units of a quaternion division algebra (all regular semisimple elements elliptic), and a torus.
routes.reason: Harish-Chandra characters, Weyl integration, the trace Paley–Wiener theorem, non-elliptic representations and Dat's ℓ-adic Langlands classification are general representation theory of p-adic groups; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups owns the smooth-representation foundations (SR.0–SR.3) but plans none of them.

ET.0 owns stable conjugacy, the transport of classes under inner twists, the cohomological parametrization of rational classes in a stable class and Kottwitz's invariants. Steinberg's lemma, the isocrystal invariant inv[b](g, g') of related elements (Kaletha, Supercuspidal L-packets via isocrystals) and the dual-group formula for the Kottwitz sign belong there; this paper is a source for them.

EDC.8 constructs cohomological correspondences and trace classes on fixed-point schemes. Varshavsky's theorem that true and naive local terms agree for automorphisms of finite prime-to-p order, and its extension to perfect schemes (Proposition 5.6.2), are statements about those local terms.
